title.value: Multi-Scale Feature Learning Dynamics: Insights for Double Descent
title.justification: The title is derived directly from the first page and header of the paper.
title.quote: MULTI - SCALE FEATURE LEARNING DYNAMICS: INSIGHTS FOR DOUBLE DESCENT

analysis.description: The paper studies the double descent phenomenon, focusing on epoch-wise double descent. It explores feature learning dynamics using a linear teacher-student model to probe generalization behaviors similar to deep neural networks. The paper provides analytical expressions to understand how features interacted during training time influences double descent behavior.

type.justification: The paper derives closed-form analytical expressions and investigates the origins of epoch-wise double descent through a theoretical model.
type.quote: By leveraging tools from statistical physics, we study a linear teacher-student setup exhibiting epoch-wise double descent similar to that in deep neural networks. In this setting, we derive closed-form analytical expressions for the evolution of generalization error over training.

name.justification: The paper primarily discusses generalization phenomena in neural networks, a core aspect of deep learning.
name.quote: A key challenge in building theoretical foundations for deep learning is the complex optimization dynamics of neural networks, resulting from the highdimensional interactions between the large number of network parameters.

name.justification: The paper investigates learning dynamics using neural networks as a reference and model.
name.quote: We validate our findings through numerical experiments where our theory accurately predicts empirical findings and remains consistent with observations in deep neural networks.

name.justification: The study uses tools from statistical physics to analyze learning dynamics.
name.quote: By leveraging tools from statistical physics, we study a linear teacher-student setup exhibiting epoch-wise double descent similar to that in deep neural networks.

name.justification: The work explores generalization phenomena, specifically the double descent of generalization error.
name.quote: Such non-trivial dynamics lead to intriguing model behaviors such as the phenomenon of “double descent” of the generalization error.

name.justification: Used in experiments to validate theoretical predictions.
name.quote: For real-world experiments, we train a ResNet18 (He et al., 2016) with large layer widths [64, 2 × 64, 4 × 64, 8 × 64].

is_contributed.justification: The paper uses a pre-existing model architecture for validation but does not contribute it as a new model.
is_contributed.quote: For real-world experiments, we train a ResNet18 (He et al., 2016) with large layer widths [64, 2 × 64, 4 × 64, 8 × 64].

is_executed.justification: The model is executed in experiments for empirical validation.
is_executed.quote: We train using Adam (Kingma & Ba, 2014) with learning rate of 1e− 4 for 1K epochs.

is_compared.justification: The paper compares empirical results with theoretical predictions.
is_compared.quote: We also conduct experiments on real-world neural networks showing a close qualitative match between the generalization behavior of neural networks and our teacher-student setup.
